slides.0.title: Central and eastern: Pic Saint-Loup, Larzac, La Clape
slides.0.subtitle: Cool uplands, coastal limestone and Muscat sweets
slides.1.title: Pic Saint-Loup
slides.1.highlights.0.title: In 2017
slides.1.highlights.0.content: VDQS in 1955, a geographic denomination within Coteaux du Languedoc in 1994 and a full AOC in January 2017; about 1,200 ha across 17 communes (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Cool and wet
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The massif reaches 658 m, vineyards average about 150 m; rainfall is about 900–1,000 mm with big diurnal swings, one of the coolest, wettest terroirs in Languedoc
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Rules
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Red and rosé only; reds at least 50% Syrah, with Syrah, Grenache and Mourvèdre together at least 90%; rosé at least 30% Syrah; Carignan and Cinsault each capped at 10%; max 50 hL/ha
slides.1.content: Whites can only be sold as AOC Languedoc, an often overlooked detail.
slides.2.title: Terrasses du Larzac
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 2004 and 2014
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A geographic denomination within Coteaux du Languedoc in 2004 and an independent AOC in 2014 (decree 2014-1200, 17 October); about 700 ha planted (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Day-night swing
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cool air from the Larzac plateau makes summer day-night swings exceed 20°C; vines sit at 50–300 m, mostly 100–150 m
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Red only
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre at least 60% together, Syrah and/or Mourvèdre at least 20%, no variety above 75%; max 45 hL/ha; at least 12% abv
slides.2.content: Larzac's yield cap (45) is lower than the Languedoc AOC red base (50).
slides.3.title: La Clape and Picpoul de Pinet
slides.3.highlights.0.title: La Clape
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Autonomous AOC on 9 June 2015; about 760 ha, less than 12 km from the sea at 20–250 m on limestone and marl (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: La Clape whites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Bourboulenc at least 40%, Grenache Blanc plus Bourboulenc at least 60%; reds need Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre at least 70% together; red is about 80%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Picpoul de Pinet
slides.3.highlights.2.content: White only, 100% Piquepoul Blanc, with its own specification from 23 September 2013; beside the Thau lagoon and known for high acid and salinity (a style generalisation)
slides.3.content: La Clape and Picpoul are among the few white-led corners of Languedoc.
slides.4.title: The Muscat sweet wines
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Frontignan
slides.4.highlights.0.content: AOC in 1936, the first of the four VDN classified as AOC; about 800 ha in Frontignan and Vic-la-Gardiole on red, iron-rich clay with limestone (wein.plus)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Similar neighbours
slides.4.highlights.1.content: To the east lies Muscat de Mireval and a little northeast Muscat de Lunel, with similar wines; Saint-Jean-de-Minervois is inland in the Minervois
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Variety
slides.4.highlights.2.content: These Muscat VDN rest on Muscat à Petits Grains (general knowledge; the wein.plus page does not state it)
slides.4.content: Languedoc's VDN are Muscat-based while Roussillon's lean on Grenache.
